issue_context.title: Allow Keyword Aggregation in DataFrame.agg and Series.agg
issue_context.body:
Followup to https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/26399

```python
In [2]: df = pd.DataFrame({"A": [1, 2, 1, 2], "B": [1, 2, 3, 4]})

In [3]: df
Out[3]:
   A  B
0  1  1
1  2  2
2  1  3
3  2  4

In [4]: df.agg(foo=("B", "sum"))
```

Expected Output

```python
In [13]: df.agg({"B": {"foo": "sum"}})
/Users/taugspurger/Envs/dask-dev/lib/python3.7/site-packages/pandas/core/frame.py:6284: FutureWarning: using a dict with renaming is deprecated and will be removed in a future version
  result, how = self._aggregate(func, axis=axis, *args, **kwargs)
Out[13]:
      B
foo  10
```


without the warning. Similar for `Series.agg`

```python
In [16]: df.B.agg({"foo": "sum"})  # allow foo="sum"
Out[16]:
foo    10
Name: B, dtype: int64
```

Is this a blocker for 0.25.0? Is anyone interested in working on it? I'm not.

cc @zertin, @smcateer, @pirsquared, who seemed interested in this for the GroupBy.agg context (this is for DataFrame/Series.agg).

I am not sure what this follow-up corresponds to.

As blocker, I remember the multiple lambda problem, for which I believe you said you had a WIP.

Which of the blocker remaining issues this issue corresponds to? The description is unclear to me.

Multiple lambdas is at https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/26905 (tagged for 0.25, but needs review).

This issue is about supporting the new named aggregation syntax in DataFrame.agg, rather than just DataFrameGroupBy.agg (likewise for Series). Ideally, these two wouldn't diverge in behavior.

```python
In [2]: df = pd.DataFrame({"A": [1, 2, 1, 2], "B": [1, 2, 3, 4]})

In [3]: df
Out[3]:
   A  B
0  1  1
1  2  2
2  1  3
3  2  4

In [4]: df.agg(foo=("B", "sum"))
      B
foo  10
```
Would be nice for 0.25, but not a blocker. Pushing.

@TomAugspurger I'm going to look into this, just had a question about desired behavior.

Currently, if you aggregate different functions on different series with `DataFrame.agg`, you still get a Series back:

```python
In [16]: df = pd.DataFrame({"A": [1, 2, 1, 2], "B": [1, 2, 3, 4]})

In [17]: df
Out[17]:
   A  B
0  1  1
1  2  2
2  1  3
3  2  4

In [18]: df.agg({"A": "sum", "B": "mean"})
Out[18]:
A    6.0
B    2.5
dtype: float64
```

For the example you provided above, it would seem the result would be something like:

```python
In [18]: df.agg(foo=("A", "sum"), bar=("B", "mean"))
Out[18]:
       A    B
foo    6  NaN
bar  NaN  2.5
```
 
When something like:

```
foo    6.0
bar    2.5
dtype: float64
```

Would be the closest to current behavior.  Any thoughts?
You're probably right about the expected output being a Series there.

Hi, @WillAyd @jreback 

I think this part has brought in quite conversations for a while, and i looked back at it again and feel there is still something could improve, so i re-designed the implementation a bit, and added quite detailed comment to explain.

The issue of `result` is, after the `self._aggregate` and `mangle_lamdbas`, if result is a `DataFrame`, the index of results will be obtained from callable name (e.g. `sum` -> `'sum'`, or `np.max` -> `'amax'`), or kept as is for string case (e.g. `'sum'` -> `'sum'`), or a parsed lambda func (e.g. `lambda x: min(x)` -> `'<lambda>'`), and index will be sorted.

so, if the call to function is `df.agg(aa=(C2, sum), ab=(C1, max), ac=(C1, np.max), ad=(C2, lambda x: min(x)), ae=(C1, sum))`, the order of functions is `C1: [max, np.max, sum]` and `C2: [sum, lambda]`, but it will look like something below in `results`:
```
             C2   C1
<lambda>      1  NaN
amax        NaN  4.0
max         NaN  4.0
sum        18.0  6.0
```
So for C2, it now has `[lambda, sum]` in result, and C1 has `[amax, max, sum]`, you can see order has changed, previously i used `[::-1]` to reorder, but this has sceanrios which cannot solve. Therefore, I decide to find the func name in index, and its position, and do a reordering for `s`, which you see in `reorder_mask` clause. And afterwards, we still need to replace those names with the names users provided in the call, e.g. `aa, ab, ae` etc, and those are unchanged in the latest commit.

The reason to have the mask is, if the result is a DataFrame and there is only one column being used for aggregation, e.g. `df.agg(aa=(C1, sum), ab=(C1, mean))`, there will be no re-sort in index, and the order is the same as called in function.

I know this might bring in a lot of confusions, but i have tried many scenarios for corner cases, seems this solution works quite good, and overall this is to achieve 3 things: 
1. the index name of aggregated dataframe has the same order of appearance as in the call, 
2. the column names of aggregated dataframes has the same order of appearance of column names as in the call, 
3. the aggregated result mapping is correct. 

Many thanks for your precious time reviewing this PR and would love to hear your feedbacks! thanks in advance! @WillAyd @jreback
